title: Masjid and Community
description: What to expect at a masjid, how to ask for help, and how to find healthy community.

sections.heading: What a Masjid Is For
sections.content: A masjid is a place for prayer, learning, community, and service. It may also host classes, youth programs, food drives, new Muslim support, and counseling referrals. Every masjid has its own culture and capacity, so one visit does not represent all Muslim community.

sections.heading: First Visit Etiquette
sections.content:
Keep the basics simple:

- Dress cleanly and modestly.
- Remove shoes where others do.
- Keep your phone quiet.
- Ask where to go if you are unsure.
- Follow the congregation during prayer as best you can.

If you make a mistake, do not panic. People are usually happy to help when they know you are new.

sections.heading: Finding a Mentor
sections.content:
A good mentor is patient, reliable, and respectful of your pace. They help with prayer, purification, Quran, community, and everyday questions without pressuring you to change everything immediately.

Ask the imam, office, or a trusted community member: **Do you have someone who helps new Muslims learn the basics?**

sections.heading: Healthy Community Signs
sections.content: Healthy community makes Islam more livable. Look for people who encourage prayer, mercy, honesty, family ties, and steady learning. Be cautious around people who isolate you, shame you constantly, demand secrecy, pressure marriage, or treat their personal culture as the whole religion.
